data.title: GM Develops Sodium-Ion Batteries to Cut Dependence on China
data.description:
According to CNBC, General Motors is in the early stages of developing next-generation battery cells that it believes can reduce U.S. dependence on China while increasing the use of domestically sourced materials. Kurt Kelty, GM's vice president of battery and sustainability, said the company is working to build a domestic supply chain over the next two to three years and wants domestic sourcing in place when the cells reach market.

GM is partnering with Denver-based startup Peak Energy on sodium-ion battery cells for energy storage systems, with commercial production expected around 2029. The automaker said it is also prioritizing domestic battery cell production for future all-electric vehicles. GM currently makes lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, cells with LG Energy Solution in the U.S. for energy storage systems, while it is producing other battery chemistries that still use undisclosed amounts of materials from China.

The company is spending $900 million on new battery lab facilities at its global tech campus in suburban Detroit, including a more than 500,000-square-foot prototyping facility set to begin operations later this year.

data.title: Market News | The 10-Year Closes at 4.974% as Markets Trade Rate Certainty Over Rate Direction
data.description: US stocks rebounded Friday after August CPI came in slightly above expectations, with the market largely confirming a Federal Reserve hike next week.The S&P 500 rose 0.9%, the Dow gained about 1% and the Nasdaq 1%. All three still ended the week lower.Investors treated a clear rate path as preferable to ambiguity — reducing policy uncertainty and avoiding more aggressive expectations later.The Mechanism Applied Across Asset ClassesThe same logic drove crypto. Bitcoin rebounded more than $3,000 from a low of $76,046 to clear $79,000, trading at $79,301 for a 24-hour gain of 2.68%.That parallel matters for interpreting both moves. Bitcoin and equities rallying together on a hawkish print is not a debasement-trade signature or a risk-on rotation. It is markets pricing the removal of a distribution of outcomes.Hike odds had been split across venues before the release — 76% on CME FedWatch, roughly two-thirds per QCP, 61% on Polymarket. A 15-point spread on a binary event indicated genuine disagreement. The print collapsed it.Core CPI rose 0.3% against 0.2% expected, the only figure in the release that missed. Headline came in at 0.4% monthly and 3.4% annually with core at 2.4% year-over-year, all in line.Yields Went the Other WayThe bond market did not participate in the relief.The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.974%, approaching the 5% threshold and up significantly from 4.783% a week earlier — a move of 19 basis points across five sessions.That divergence is the session's most important detail. Equities and Bitcoin rallied on reduced uncertainty while the asset that actually prices the rate path pushed toward a psychological level it has not breached this cycle.A 5% handle on the 10-year would be the first since 2007. QCP framed the problem for Bitcoin specifically before the print: "This is the worst mix for Bitcoin: a competing 5% risk-free rate without the nominal-growth impulse that usually accompanies yield moves."RBC Moved From Cuts to Three HikesThe forecast revision quantifies how far the outlook has shifted.RBC Capital Markets revised its expectations for this year from rate cuts to three rate hikes, warning that high rates could further weigh on corporate earnings and equity valuations.That is a reversal of direction rather than a recalibration of magnitude. A house expecting easing at the start of the period now expects 75 basis points of tightening.Markets currently price a 25 basis point move at next week's meeting. Rates have sat at 3.50%-3.75% since December 2025, making a September increase the first since July 2023.Saudi Arabia Closed the East-West PipelineThe energy picture deteriorated further, and one development deserves more attention than it received.Brent closed at $104.61, up more than 8% on the week. Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities and transportation risks in the Strait of Hormuz contributed, but Saudi Arabia's closure of the East-West pipeline is the structurally significant item.That pipeline runs from the Eastern Province oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, and its entire strategic purpose is providing an export route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Closing it removes the alternative.With Hormuz shipping disrupted and the bypass shut, Saudi crude has no unconstrained path to market. That is the mechanical explanation for production falling 1.9 million barrels per day to 6.238 million — the lowest since 1990. A producer that cannot export cannot sustain output.The Question Has Shifted From Direction to DurationWall Street's framing has moved from whether the Fed will raise rates to how long high rates persist, and whether inflation can be contained without damaging the economy and corporate earnings.That reframing changes what matters at Wednesday's meeting. The decision itself is largely priced. The dot plot, the updated projections and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference carry the information.Warsh has rejected forward guidance as a practice, which complicates the market's need for exactly that. The Wall Street Journal's Nick Timiraos identified the bind before CPI: the Jackson Hole speech convinced investors a hike was likelier without specifying a trigger, leaving a single data release to authorize a decision Warsh has argued against making that way.The same absence of guidance now applies to the duration question.High Oil and High Rates Together Keep Volatility ElevatedThe combination is what keeps the outlook unstable regardless of Friday's recovery.Elevated crude feeds inflation, which supports higher rates, which compresses valuations — while the energy shock simultaneously pressures corporate margins from the cost side. Neither variable resolves the other.For crypto, the demand picture entering the weekend had not turned. CryptoQuant's spot demand metric sits at −145,000 BTC after nearly reaching positive at −5,000 in late August. The Coinbase premium index fell to −0.036. Crypto ETFs saw $308 million of net outflows Thursday, the worst single day in two months.Spot Bitcoin ETF trading pauses until Monday, and the Clarity Act cloture vote falls September 15 with the Fed decision the following day.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Iraq Removes Maysan Commander After Drone Strikes on Saudi Pipeline
data.description:
Iraq dismissed the commander of Maysan province after drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline were determined to have been launched from inside Iraq, according to Bloomberg.

The pipeline closure triggered further fallout on Saturday.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | BRICS Urge Maximum Restraint as Middle East Tensions Rise
data.description: BRICS nations including Iran and the United Arab Emirates said they were deeply concerned about escalating tensions in the Middle East and called for maximum restraint in a joint statement published on Saturday, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | Skyworth Digital Sees Smart Terminal Growth Supported by Three Factors
data.description: According to Jin10, Skyworth Digital said at its earnings briefing that the core driver of its first-half performance growth came from a broad recovery in its smart terminal business, which generated revenue of 4.4 billion yuan, up 52.45% year on year, with sales volume, revenue scale, and gross margin all rising together. The company said the growth was supported by three factors: intensive rollout of operator bulk-purchase projects, with shipments of its Smart Lingxi screen exceeding 300,000 units; continued optimization of its product mix, as it voluntarily gave up some low-gross-margin traditional bulk-purchase orders and focused on higher-value-added products; and strong overseas expansion, with the Nex Playground motion-sensing game console posting standout sales in North America. Skyworth Digital said it remains upbeat on full-year performance as operator bulk-purchase projects continue to be delivered in the second half, overseas peak-season sales begin, and vehicle display and other projects gradually enter mass production.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Oil Surge Lifts Global Inflation Pressures
data.description:
Inflation pressures intensified across the global economy this week as surging energy costs from the Iran war continued to feed through to consumer and producer prices, according to Bloomberg.

The move raised the risk of slower growth and tighter monetary policy.

data.title: STOCKS | Mike Wilson Warns Oil Prices Could Trigger S&P 500 Correction Within 30 Days
data.description:
Mike Wilson said oil prices could trigger an S&P 500 correction within 30 days if crude rises to $120 to $140 a barrel. According to NS3.AI, he said that range could drain market liquidity.

Wilson remained bullish on stocks, saying valuations have adjusted and earnings growth continues to support indexes.

data.title: Clarity Act Faces Procedural Vote on September 15, Trump Crypto Adviser Says
data.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's digital assets advisory council executive director Patrick Witt told Semafor that the window of opportunity for the Clarity Act is closing. According to PANews, Witt said that if next week's procedural vote fails, no one can say when the bill will get another chance. Witt said a failed motion vote would not give anyone the outcome they want and called for bipartisan support for the bill. The procedural vote is scheduled for September 15.

data.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Foil Assassination Plot, Kill 4 Militants
data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Quds Force said on September 12 that it killed four militants who were trying to carry out an assassination plot in the Saravan area of Sistan and Baluchestan Province in southeastern Iran. The statement said the Revolutionary Guards, together with intelligence agencies and law enforcement forces, launched an operation against the group early that morning, killing the four militants on the spot and seizing weapons, ammunition, and explosives at their hideout. Three Revolutionary Guards members were killed in the operation.

data.title: Hidden Crypto Farm Found in Puebla With 300 GPUs, Authorities Say
data.description: Mexican authorities discovered a hidden crypto farm in Puebla equipped with 300 graphics processing units. According to NS3.AI, the site was suspected of mining virtual coins to launder illicit funds. It was the fourth such farm found in the area since early last year.

data.title: HDFC Bank Submits Two Candidates to Reserve Bank of India for MD and CEO Role
data.description:
HDFC Bank said it has submitted the names of two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India for the position of managing director and chief executive officer.

Bloomberg posted on X, citing the bank’s disclosure about the leadership search.

The bank did not provide further details on the candidates or the timeline for the appointment.

data.title: Nasdaq Agrees to Invest $100 Million in Payward for Tokenized Equity Infrastructure
data.description:
Nasdaq has agreed to invest $100 million in Payward to help develop infrastructure for tokenized equities. According to NS3.AI, London Stock Exchange Group also partnered with Payward on tokenized UK shares.

RWA.xyz tracked $2.91 billion in distributed tokenized stocks as of September 10. Holder numbers rose 174% over 30 days.

data.title: Iranian President Meets Abu Dhabi Crown Prince in New Delhi
data.description: According to Jin10, the Iranian Embassy in India said the Iranian president met the Abu Dhabi crown prince in New Delhi, India.

data.title: Donut AI CEO Chris Reveals On-Chain Trading Portfolio and Strategy
data.description:
Donut AI CEO and founder Chris publicly disclosed his on-chain investment portfolio and trading approach, according to on-chain analyst Ai Yi. The portfolio includes PUMP, PONS, AI, BONER, and STONK.

According to ChainCatcher, Chris has held PUMP for several months and has made more than $936,000 in cumulative profit. He also earned more than $130,000 from trading popular Robinhood Chain tokens over the past 30 days, including exiting PONS when its market value was about $600 million.

Chris said he opened a position in STONK when its market value was about $89 million and is now sitting on about $180,000 in unrealized gains, representing a return of more than 170%. He said Robinhood Chain currently relies more on new retail inflows, while Solana has a larger base of on-chain capital, making him more optimistic about the long-term development of Solana's tokenized stock ecosystem.

data.title: Trump Says Iran-Backed Houthis Asked the U.S. Not to Intervene
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump said the Iran-backed Houthis had asked the United States not to attack the militant group. According to Sina Finance, Trump told reporters on Saturday during a meeting in Dublin with Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin that the Houthis “called us and they don’t want to fight us,” adding that they “very much hope that we don’t go in.”

Trump said he had spoken with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman but did not provide details. He also said, “I can only say everything will work out fine. The result will be very good.”

data.title: Russia Shifts Grain Exports to Far East as Black Sea Ports Face Strikes
data.description: Russia is using its Far East as an alternative route to export grain after Ukrainian strikes disrupted shipments from key Black Sea ports, Agriculture Minister Oksana Lut said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Jewish Communities' Security Costs Top $1 Billion A Year
data.description:
According to Axios, Jewish communal institutions in the United States are spending an estimated $1.02 billion a year on security, a record high, according to new data from the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA). The estimate is up 33% from $765 million in 2024 and covers more than 4,500 synagogues, Jewish community centers, schools, summer camps and other nonprofits, which spend an average of about $225,000 each. Security personnel account for the largest share, while about $150 million goes to security technology and building hardening, including cameras, reinforced doors and controlled-entry systems. The estimate does not include costs at more than 1,600 kosher restaurants, about 500 kosher markets and groceries, or other privately owned Jewish businesses.

Axios reported that the higher spending comes as antisemitic assaults have reached their highest level since the Anti-Defamation League began tracking them in 1979. Community Security Service CEO Richard Priem said there is now more capability protecting the Jewish community than there was a few years ago, while JFNA CEO Eric Fingerhut said every dollar spent on guards and cameras is a dollar not spent on Jewish education. The article also said FEMA has made $300 million available through the FY 2026 Nonprofit Security Grant Program, and that a bipartisan bill in Congress would authorize $1 billion annually from FY 2027 through FY 2031 for the program and loosen limits on using the money for security personnel.

data.title: Tahe Music Receives CSRC Overseas Listing Feedback on Hong Kong IPO Filing
data.description:
Tahe Music has received feedback from China's securities regulator on its overseas listing filing, with the China Securities Regulatory Commission's International Department asking the company to supplement disclosures and have lawyers verify the matters and issue clear legal opinions, according to Jiemian News. The questions cover the paid-in status of domestic operating entities' registered capital, the basis for past capital increases and equity transfers, whether any capital contribution obligations were unmet, whether there were nominee shareholding arrangements, and whether the company's domestic business involves foreign investment restricted or prohibited sectors.

The regulator also asked Tahe Music to explain the compliance of its offshore structure and round-trip investment, including foreign exchange, outbound investment, foreign investment and tax procedures, as well as the fairness of transaction consideration and whether related transferors fulfilled tax filing obligations. It further requested details on the legality of the equity incentive plan, possible benefit transfers or disputes, the use of a trust structure, and the basic information of the trust and related domestic entities. In addition, the company was asked to disclose the circumstances and rectification measures related to administrative penalties imposed on Chengdu Tahe by the Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Culture, Radio, Television and Tourism, and to clarify whether the Hong Kong listing is a spin-off of a Nasdaq- and Hong Kong-listed company and, if so, whether the parent and spun-off unit are operationally independent.

data.title: Russia’s Rosatom Plans to Increase Experts at Iran’s Bushehr Nuclear Plant to 150
data.description: According to Jin10, Russia’s state nuclear company Rosatom said it plans to increase the number of experts at Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant to 150 in the near future.
